newsitem.title: ITALY: Meridiana says "no interest in cargo", boosts MD-8.
newsitem.headline: Meridiana says "no interest in cargo", boosts MD-8.

text.p: Italy's private sector Meridiana airline does not intend to further develop its air cargo interests, Meridiana vice-president Steve Forte told a news conference.
The airline: "is not interested in cargo" and "we have chosen not to invest resources in developing this market," he added.
The carrier said that its fleet renewal operations will continue this year and in June it will receive a McDonnell Douglas MD-82, its 19th aircraft.
At present it operates eight MD-82, six DC9-51s as well as four BAe 146 used for the restricted access airport at Florence.
Between 1998 and end-2000, the airline will have replaced all the DC9-51s with six MD-82s giving it a total of 15 MD-82s.
It added that the passenger load factor for 1996 fell to 53.6 percent from 56 percent a year earlier.
The airline also confirmed details of two code-sharing agreements starting on June 1 with Alitalia and France's Air Littoral.

Under the deal with Italy's state carrier, the two airlines will offer 50 seats on each other's twice daily flights on two routes. The first is Turin-Catania-Turin operated by Meridiana and the second is Bologna-Palermo-Bologna provided by Alitalia.,
The agreement with Air Littoral will give Meridiana 43 seats -- out of 46 - on ATR42 flights between Nice-Olbia-Nice.

It has also signed a deal with Spain's Spanair effective June 1 under which Meridiana passengers on daily flights to Barcelona from Bologna and Florence can transfer to Madrid on Spanair aircraft. --Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542-7706 Fax+5017
